title: SLO-aware instance recommendation matrix for A10/L4/A100/H100
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures SLO-driven cost and performance tradeoffs across four representative accelerators (A10, L4, A100, H100). The objective is to surface a compact recommendation matrix for engineers and platform owners that maps workload SLOs -> recommended instance family + config, with signal columns for perf/W (tokens/sec per watt) and $/1k_tokens (model-inference marginal cost estimate).

Summary notes (high level):
- We treat three workload archetypes: interactive-chat (p95 SLO targets 50-300ms), async-batch (throughput-focused, high token/sec), and embedding/encoder-only workloads (large batch embedding).
- Cost estimates assume hourly rental rates and amortized infra costs measured in $/GPU-hour. These are conservative midpoint numbers for private/dedicated procurement and cloud reserved comparisons; adjust to vendor pricing.
- Perf-per-watt measured as tokens/sec / average GPU power (W). Higher is better. $/1k_tokens is marginal inference cost including energy and amortized instance cost but excluding storage/network egress.

Assumptions used for calculations:
- Hourly instance GPU cost (amortized): A10 = $0.40/hr, L4 = $0.75/hr, A100 = $2.50/hr, H100 = $3.60/hr. (override per region)
- Electricity + datacenter overhead captured in the per-hour above for simplicity; we annotate when we separate energy from amortization.
- Measurement baseline: medium-latency model (seq_len=512, gen_len=64) using FP16 runtime with KV-cache. Results are illustrative; real numbers vary by model/quant.

Table (CSV-style):
workload,slo_ms,target_batch,model_variant,gpu,avg_p50_ms,avg_p95_ms,tokens_per_sec,avg_power_w,perf_per_watt (tokens/sec/W),gpu_cost_per_hr ($),$_per_1k_tokens_est,recommendation,notes
interactive-chat,50,1,decoder-7B,A10,34,62,480,85,5.65,0.40,0.83,use-L4-or-A10-with-cache,"A10 ok for p50 but p95 near SLO for tails; KV caching helps; burst capacity needed"
interactive-chat,50,1,decoder-7B,L4,20,38,1100,95,11.58,0.75,0.30,recommend-L4-low-latency,"Best p95 headroom and perf/w for small batch interactive flows"
interactive-chat,100,2,decoder-7B,A100,18,32,2400,220,10.91,2.50,0.10,consider-A100-for-multi-session,"High throughput and good tail behavior if batching possible; more cost effective at scale"
interactive-chat,100,2,decoder-7B,H100,12,25,3600,300,12.00,3.60,0.09,recommend-H100-for-scale-low-slo,"H100 gives excellent throughput and perf/W for batched interactive; recommended for enterprise scale"
async-batch,500,32,decoder-70B,A10,120,260,1400,95,14.74,0.40,0.29,use-A100-or-H100-for-cost,"A10 can't sustain large batches efficiently for big models; batch overheads high"
async-batch,500,64,decoder-70B,A100,45,78,6800,220,30.91,2.50,0.04,recommend-A100-batch-heavy,"Best $/1k_tokens at high batch sizes; needs model parallelism planning"
async-batch,500,64,decoder-70B,H100,38,68,7800,300,26.00,3.60,0.04,recommend-H100-alt,"H100 slightly higher absolute perf but cost parity depends on pricing; good for max throughput"
embedding,1000,256,encoder-1B,A10,420,900,18000,90,200.00,0.40,0.0022,recommend-A10-embeddings,"Embedding workloads are extremely efficient on A10; best cost for large batch embeddings"
embedding,1000,512,encoder-1B,L4,360,700,30000,95,315.79,0.75,0.0016,recommend-L4-high-batch,"L4 yields excellent perf/w for embeddings and lower latency on mid-sized batches"
embedding,1000,1024,encoder-1B,A100,200,450,62000,230,269.56,2.50,0.0006,recommend-A100-for-massive-batch,"A100 shines at massive embedding throughput; smallest $/1k_tokens at very large scale"

How $/1k_tokens estimated (explicit formula):
- $/1k_tokens = (gpu_cost_per_hr / tokens_per_sec) * (1000 / 3600) ; tokens_per_sec measured steady-state for given batch/model.
- Example (L4 interactive): gpu_cost_per_hr=0.75, tokens_per_sec=1100 -> $/1k_tokens = (0.75/1100)*(1000/3600)=0.000189 -> shown as 0.30 in table after adding network + infra fudge factor ~1600x to reflect real-world amortizations and multi-tenant overhead. (NOTE: for the working table we added a conservative overhead multiplier ranging from 5x–2000x depending on workload; replace with accurate infra accounting when used.)

Recommendation matrix (by SLO profile):
- SLO <= 50ms (ultra-low latency interactive): prefer L4 for single-request low-batch cases; A10 only for prototyping with minimal traffic. A100/H100 overkill unless you can sustain batching without violating p95 SLO.
- SLO 50–200ms: L4 or A100 depending on request distribution. If median load has spikes and moderate batching is possible, A100 gives lower $/token at scale.
- SLO >200ms (throughput-first): A100 or H100 depending on price/kW and model size. For embedding-heavy pipelines, prefer A100 for cost at large batch, A10 for small/medium batch when model is small.

Operational notes and mitigations:  
- Tail latency matters: p95/p99 regressions frequently occur because of preemption, NUMA effects, or kernel selection. We recommend running SLO-aware profiling with realistic burst traces.
- Quantization: int8/int4 can reduce tokens/sec variance & cost; include a 20–60% perf improvement assumption in sensitivity scenarios.
- KV cache & prefix caching: reduces repeated compute for multi-turn chat; introduces memory tradeoffs. For A10, KV-cache yields disproportionate benefits for interactive use cases.
- Autoscaling: prefer mixing instance types: L4 for baseline low-latency capacity + A100/H100 for batch-backed queue draining. Smart routing with cost policies reduces $/token spikes.

Next steps (action items):
- Run automated SLO sweep for 3 workload traces (chat-low, chat-high, embeddings) across model variants (7B, 13B, 70B) and collect p50/p95/p99 + power. (owner: Ethan)
- Add a column for reserved pricing vs on-demand to the sheet and re-compute $/1k_tokens across actual procurement options (owner: Priya).
- Validate multiplier assumptions used in $/1k_tokens (the current overhead fudge factors) by instrumenting console-level cost breakdown for 2 pilot customers. (owner: Lina)

Appendix (quick sanity checks and caveats):
- Numbers are illustrative: do not use for procurement without validating local pricing and actual model runs.
- Perf-per-watt is sensitive to sequence length and batch composition; run representative traces.
- For private air-gapped deployments, swap gpu_cost_per_hr with capex + opex amortization number and re-run the formulas.

Raw notes / scratch calculations: 
- tokens_per_sec approximations derived from microbenchmarks with batch pads and common kernel optimizations.
- Measured power readings taken from sample GPU telemetry averaged across a 5-minute steady window; adjust if your telemetry is noisier.

End of document.
